Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

This patient with oesophageal cancer and underlying Hashimoto's thyroiditis (2019: elevated antibodies, ultrasound changes) was euthyroid in April 2022 (TT4 53.87, TSH 0.82) before starting pembrolizumab-based chemotherapy on 15 April 2022.

The thyroid trajectory shows a classic biphasic pattern consistent with checkpoint-inhibitor-induced thyroiditis: a transient thyrotoxic phase on 6 May 2022 (TT4 164.49, TSH <0.004) representing destructive release of stored hormone, followed by a severe hypothyroid phase in August–September 2022 (TT4 <3.9, TSH 119.96; TT4 31.2, TSH 71.86) on 100 mcg levothyroxine. By 27 October 2022, values had normalised on the same 100 mcg dose (TT4 68.0, TSH 2.36).

The dose was then increased to 125 mcg, after which TSH became suppressed (0.06 in November, 0.08 in January) with TT4 falling below the reference interval (45.8 in January). This represents over-replacement.

Prioritised interpretations:
1. Pembrolizumab-induced thyroiditis (destructive, biphasic) superimposed on Hashimoto's — most likely given the temporal relationship and classic pattern.
2. The current TSH suppression reflects an excessive dose increase made after the patient had already normalised on 100 mcg.
3. Ongoing pembrolizumab (continued after chemotherapy) may sustain immune-mediated thyroid injury, making future hypothyroid relapse possible.

Next steps: Consider reducing levothyroxine back to 100 mcg (or even 75 mcg) with repeat TSH/TT4 in 6–8 weeks. Monitor for recurrence of hypothyroidism given continued pembrolizumab. The dose was then increased to 125 mcg, after which TSH became suppressed (0.06 November, 0.08 January) with TT4 below reference (45.8 January).
